explanation: To be WEARY is to have one's strength used up, i.e. to be "tired".
distractor_rationales: "bored" is the mind running out of interest rather than the body running out of strength
"hungry" is a bodily want of a different kind — food, not rest
"restless" names the inability to settle, which is the opposite state of body from being worn out
"lonely" is a want of company rather than a want of rest
KEY

explanation: A slice is a portion deliberately cut out of the loaf so that the whole may be shared out; "wedge is to pie" is the same cut-portion-to-whole pair.
distractor_rationales: "crumb is to cake" is a fragment that falls off, not a portion cut to be served
"segment is to orange" is a division the fruit already grows, not one the knife makes
KEY
"crust is to bread" is the outer layer of the loaf rather than a portion of it
"core is to apple" is an interior structure, and it is the part discarded rather than the part served

explanation: To be VIGILANT is to keep a close and constant lookout, which "watchful" names exactly.
distractor_rationales: "hopeful" is an expectation about the future, not an attention paid to the present
KEY
"truthful" is about what one says rather than what one notices
"boastful" concerns the figure one cuts in one’s own account of oneself, not what one keeps an eye on
"graceful" describes the manner of a movement, not the keeping of a watch

explanation: A dictionary is a reference volume that sets out the whole class of items in a fixed order so any one can be looked up; "atlas is to maps" is the same reference-volume-to-contents pair.
distractor_rationales: KEY
"album is to photographs" is a keepsake collection kept for its own sake, with no order built for looking a thing up
"scrapbook is to clippings" gathers whatever happened to be saved rather than the whole class of items
"anthology is to poems" is a selection made for merit, so it is deliberately not exhaustive
"ledger is to transactions" records events as they occurred rather than cataloguing a class of things

explanation: TREPIDATION is the nervous dread felt before something one must face, which "alarm" names most closely.
distractor_rationales: "fatigue" is the body's exhaustion, not a fear
KEY
"boredom" is an absence of interest where trepidation is an excess of concern
"curiosity" also points forward to what is coming, but draws one toward it rather than making one shrink
"resentment" is a grievance held about what has already happened

explanation: A feather is one of the many small overlapping units that together make up the bird's covering; "scale is to fish" is the same single-unit-to-animal pair.
distractor_rationales: "fur is to rabbit" names the covering in the mass; there is no single unit of it that one could point to
KEY
"wool is to sheep" likewise names the whole fleece rather than one unit of it
"shell is to turtle" is a covering made of a single piece, not of many repeated units
"mane is to lion" covers one region of the animal rather than being a unit of its covering

explanation: A BLUNDER is a clumsy error, so "mistake" is the closest word.
distractor_rationales: "promise" is an undertaking about the future, unrelated to a slip already made
"insult" is a deliberate wounding, where a blunder is done without meaning to
"delay" is a setback in time and may follow a blunder without being one
"excuse" is what is offered after the error rather than the error itself
KEY

explanation: A recipe is a written specification the cook works through step by step in order to produce the finished dish; "score is to musician" is the same instructions-to-performer pair.
distractor_rationales: "menu is to diner" offers a set of choices, and the diner makes nothing from it
"map is to traveler" sets out the ground rather than a sequence of steps to be executed in order
"timetable is to commuter" is consulted for a fact rather than followed through as a procedure
"diary is to novelist" records what has happened instead of directing what is to be made
KEY

explanation: Something STURDY is solidly built and hard to break, i.e. "strong".
distractor_rationales: KEY
"smooth" describes the surface rather than how well the thing holds together
"noisy" is a matter of sound, not of build
"heavy" confuses weight with strength; a sturdy thing need not be heavy
"tall" is a dimension, and height gives no account of how solidly a thing is made

explanation: A fuse is the part built to give way first when the load runs too high, so that the circuit behind it survives; "valve is to boiler" is the same sacrificial-release-to-system pair.
distractor_rationales: KEY
"lock is to door" keeps others out rather than releasing a dangerous excess from within
"brake is to car" is worked deliberately by the driver instead of yielding on its own when a limit is passed
"anchor is to ship" holds the vessel in place and is not spent to save it
"railing is to staircase" guards the person using the system rather than the system itself

explanation: A JOVIAL person is hearty and full of good humor, which "cheerful" captures.
distractor_rationales: "curious" is an appetite for knowing rather than a disposition of mood
"generous" is open-handedness with what one owns, a different warmth from good humor
KEY
"patient" names the willingness to wait, which says nothing about spirits
"humble" is a low estimate of oneself, which a jovial person may or may not hold

explanation: The hull is the sealed outer body that encloses the whole vessel and gives it its shape; "fuselage is to airplane" is the same enclosing-body-to-craft pair.
distractor_rationales: "keel is to yacht" runs along the bottom as a spine; it is a member of the body, not the body
"chassis is to automobile" is the frame carried inside the body rather than the shell that encloses it
"mast is to schooner" projects out of the vessel instead of enclosing it
KEY
"cabin is to houseboat" is a space within the craft rather than the skin around it

explanation: To EQUIVOCATE is to speak in a way that avoids committing oneself either way, i.e. to "hedge".
distractor_rationales: "chatter" is talking at length about little, which is not the same as talking so as not to be pinned down
"repeat" says the same thing again; the equivocator's trouble is saying two things at once
"recite" delivers a fixed text from memory, which commits one to every word of it
KEY
"greet" is an opening courtesy and takes no position at all to be evasive about

explanation: A mitten is a soft knitted garment drawn over the hand so that the whole of it is enclosed; "sock is to foot" is the same sheathing-garment-to-limb pair.
distractor_rationales: "ring is to finger" is a band on one digit, and it is jewelry rather than a covering
"hat is to head" rests on top and leaves the face uncovered rather than enclosing the whole part
"scarf is to neck" is wound round loosely rather than made to the shape of the part
"belt is to waist" encircles a line of the body and covers nothing
KEY

explanation: To SCOFF is to speak of something with open contempt, which "sneer" names.
distractor_rationales: "stammer" is a stumbling delivery, a fault of fluency rather than an attitude
"whisper" describes how softly one speaks, not the scorn in it
KEY
"mumble" is indistinct speech and may carry any attitude at all
"chant" is repeated rhythmic utterance, which fixes the form of the speech rather than its contempt

explanation: A census is the exhaustive count, one by one, of everybody present at a single moment; "inventory is to stock" is the same complete-enumeration-to-subject pair.
distractor_rationales: "audit is to accounts" tests whether a record is correct rather than counting what is there
KEY
"poll is to opinion" questions a sample and reasons from it to the whole, where a census leaves nobody out
"forecast is to weather" predicts a future state instead of recording a present one
"survey is to land" measures extent and boundary rather than counting a number of items

explanation: MURKY water is dark and clouded so that one cannot see through it, i.e. "cloudy".
distractor_rationales: "salty" is taste and content rather than clearness
"chilly" is a matter of temperature, not of what can be seen through the water
"shallow" is depth; shallow water is often the clearest
KEY
"narrow" describes the width of the channel and says nothing about the water in it

explanation: A blush is the involuntary bodily sign that gives away the feeling even when one is trying to hide it; "tremble is to fear" is the same involuntary-sign-to-feeling pair.
distractor_rationales: "sigh is to relief" is largely within the sigher's control and serves as much to tell others as to betray oneself
"smile is to joy" can be produced at will, so it is no proof of the feeling behind it
"yawn is to boredom" follows as readily from a poor night's sleep as from tedium
KEY
"wince is to pain" answers a sensation in the body rather than a feeling about oneself

explanation: To RELISH something is to take keen pleasure in it, i.e. to "enjoy" it.
distractor_rationales: "recall" brings the thing back to mind without any pleasure being taken in it
KEY
"postpone" puts the thing off, where relishing is done in the thing's presence
"permit" allows the thing to happen and is consistent with disliking it
"notice" is bare awareness, the least any pleasure could be built on

explanation: A crown is worn as the insignia by which the office is recognized and does no practical work; "badge is to constable" is the same worn-insignia-to-office pair.
distractor_rationales: "apron is to blacksmith" is likewise worn for protection from the work
"gavel is to judge" is a tool taken up to do a piece of the work, and it is not worn
"helmet is to soldier" is worn but is protective gear, not a mark of rank
KEY
"whistle is to referee" is an instrument sounded to make a ruling rather than an emblem of holding the post

explanation: A GRIMY surface is coated with ingrained dirt, so "filthy" is the closest word.
distractor_rationales: KEY
"faded" is color lost to light rather than dirt laid on
"sticky" describes how a surface behaves to the touch, which grime need not
"damp" is held moisture, and a grimy thing is as often bone dry
"chipped" is damage to the shape of the thing rather than anything upon it

explanation: A tributary is a smaller channel whose traffic of water runs into the larger one and is carried on by it; "lane is to highway" is the same feeder-to-main-route pair.
distractor_rationales: "twig is to bough" divides outward from the larger part instead of delivering anything into it
KEY
"corridor is to hall" opens onto the larger space, but the hall does not carry the corridor's traffic onward
"suburb is to city" is a district of the whole rather than a channel joining it
"alcove is to room" is a recess off the larger space and is a dead end

explanation: Something INSIPID has no flavor or interest in it at all, which "dull" names.
distractor_rationales: "solemn" is a gravity of manner, which is a definite character of its own rather than the want of one
"harsh" is a strong quality strongly felt, not the want of one
KEY
"modest" is also an absence of display, but it is a restraint chosen rather than a want of substance
"abrupt" concerns the suddenness of a manner rather than whether there is anything in it

explanation: A scabbard is worn on the person and holds the one weapon so that it can be drawn at a moment's notice; "holster is to pistol" is the same worn-sheath-to-weapon pair.
distractor_rationales: "case is to violin" is carried rather than worn, and it is opened at leisure
"quiver is to arrows" holds a supply of many rather than a single weapon
KEY
"sleeve is to record" protects a thing in storage, and nothing is drawn from it in haste
"wallet is to banknotes" carries a number of items, and what it holds is not an implement to be used

explanation: To QUARREL is to fall into angry dispute with somebody, i.e. to "argue".
distractor_rationales: "boast" is speech about oneself and wants no opponent
"bargain" is also a two-sided exchange of words, but it is conducted to reach a deal rather than in anger
"complain" can be done alone and needs nobody to answer back
"apologize" is what may be said to close a quarrel rather than what happens in one
KEY

explanation: A verdict is the authoritative judgment that the trial exists in order to produce and that formally closes it; "diagnosis is to examination" is the same judgment-to-procedure pair.
distractor_rationales: "invoice is to purchase" is a record of what took place, not a finding about it
"score is to game" is a tally accumulated throughout rather than a judgment handed down at the end
"armistice is to war" halts the fighting by agreement without settling who was in the right
KEY
"moral is to fable" is drawn afterward by the reader and is no part of what the fable is conducted to produce

explanation: A PLIABLE material bends readily without breaking, which "flexible" names.
distractor_rationales: "reusable" is about how many times it may serve, not how it behaves under bending
"valuable" is worth rather than a physical property of the material
"portable" is about being carried, which has to do with weight and bulk rather than bending
"washable" concerns how the material stands up to water
KEY

explanation: An alibi is the evidence the accused produces afterward to show that a particular act cannot be laid at their door; "receipt is to buyer" is the same evidence-clearing-its-holder pair.
distractor_rationales: KEY
"passport is to traveler" certifies who the holder is rather than what the holder did
"license is to driver" grants a permission in advance instead of answering a charge after the fact
"testimony is to witness" is an account given about others and does not clear the one who gives it
"uniform is to officer" shows the standing the wearer holds, not a fact about any particular occasion

explanation: To ACQUIESCE is to give in and go along with what is proposed, i.e. to "consent".
distractor_rationales: KEY
"inquire" asks after the proposal rather than accepting it
"hesitate" is to hang back from answering, which withholds the agreement rather than giving it
"withdraw" takes oneself out of the matter instead of falling in with it
"pretend" concerns whether one is sincere and leaves open whether one agreed at all

explanation: A CIRCUITOUS route goes round about instead of straight to the point, which "winding" describes.
distractor_rationales: "crowded" is how much traffic is on it, which is no part of its route
"unpaved" is the surface of the road rather than the shape of its course
KEY
"scenic" is what can be seen from the road; an indirect road often is, but need not be
"uphill" is the road's gradient, a matter of climbing rather than of going round
